title: Smart routing fallback - incident breadcrumbs (Lee)
content:
High-level: brief breadcrumbs from on-call/debug session investigating smart-routing fallback that caused elevated error rates and increased latency for customers in eu-west1 -> observed traffic routed to us-east1 fallback path. Notes are rough; use for follow-up and triage.

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 2025-11-02 15:23 - First Pager: elevated 5xx rate for model-embed-r1 in eu-west1 (alerts from per-route error-rate rule).
- 15:25 - Oncall (Ethan) acknowledged, started runbook.
- 15:32 - Confirmed spikes correlate with smart-routing policy triggering fallback to region us-east1 for ~20% of requests.
- 15:40 - Temporary mitigation: disabled fallback for affected customer route (route-id: r-8f2c) via console; immediate drop in 5xx observed but latency for remaining requests in eu-west1 increased.

Commands & checks run (copyable):
- curl healthcheck to routers in eu-west1:
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" https://router.eu-west1.redwood/api/v1/health
  -> 200 0.12s (ok for controller, but some upstreams show degraded).

- Router debug: get routing decisions for sample request-id:
  curl -s -H "X-Request-ID: req-20251102-abc" "https://router.eu-west1.redwood/internal/debug?route=r-8f2c"
  -> output shows: policy=smart-routing, decision=fallback, fallback_target=us-east1, reason=active-capacity-threshold

- Grep logs for ModelUnavailable error (kibana query):
  service:inference AND message:/ModelUnavailableError/ AND region:eu-west1
  -> multiple traces around 15:20-15:30: "ModelUnavailableError: no healthy endpoints for model-embed-r1 (capacity exhausted)"

- Check node utilization (k8s side):
  kubectl -n inference get pods -l region=eu-west1 -o wide
  kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/router-xyz -- sh -c "ps aux | grep router"
  -> several pods OOM/killed prior day; node autoscaler showed delayed scale-up, some pods in CrashLoopBackOff earlier today (confirm events).

Observed error snippets (copied):
- "ModelUnavailableError: no healthy endpoints for model-embed-r1"
- "RouterDecision: fallback -> us-east1 ; reason=active-capacity-threshold ; threshold=0.8 ; current=0.92"
- "KV cache miss spike: kv-cache.get latency_p50=18ms (baseline 3ms)"

Hypotheses:
- H1: Burst capacity exceeded in eu-west1 (real traffic surge) -> active-capacity-threshold triggered fallback. Autoscaler failed to respond fast enough due to conservative cooldown or scale limits.
- H2: One or more model-serving nodes were unhealthy (OOMs after recent container image change) causing less available capacity than we thought.
- H3: Router policy TTL/weight calculation bug: recent change to smart-routing weight smoothing made fallback more aggressive on short spikes. See PR-429 for changes.
- H4: KV cache degradation in eu-west1 caused higher latency which made router mark endpoints unhealthy prematurely.

What we changed during incident (mitigations):
- 15:40 - Disabled fallback for route r-8f2c (console) to stop cross-region tail latency. Immediate reduction in 5xx from that customer but overall eu-west1 errors persisted for new requests.
- 15:55 - Increased min replicas for model-embed-r1 in eu-west1 (k8s scale to 6 -> monitor). Saw gradual recovery over 10m.
- 16:10 - Reverted container image that was rolled out yesterday to previous stable (rollback PR applied). Observed fewer OOMs after rollback.
- 16:30 - Re-enabled fallback with conservative threshold (0.95) for staging routes to test behavior.

Follow-ups & TODOs (owners suggested):
- ACTION: product/infra (Marcus) - review autoscaler config: reduce scaleDown/scaleUp cooldowns; verify cluster autoscaler quotas in eu-west1. (Jira: INC-3421 follow-up).
- ACTION: serving (Olivia) - audit recent image changes for embed model; run soak-test for memory regressions.
- ACTION: routing (Lee) - add histogram + alert for "fallback rate" per-route (not just errors) so we detect fallbacks earlier; add dashboard tile.
- ACTION: ops (Ethan) - confirm kv-cache cluster health metrics have appropriate SLOs; add alert when p95 latency > 10ms for 1m.

Notes for postmortem:
- Root cause appears to be cascading: degraded hosts (OOMs after new image) reduced capacity -> autoscaler didn't compensate quickly -> router smart-routing considered endpoints unhealthy and triggered fallback -> cross-region fallback increased tail latency for some customers -> disabling fallback stopped cross-region errors but left local errors until scale/rollback.
- Risk: aggressive fallback can mask capacity problems but can also surface cross-region latency/cost. Need better guardrails (circuit-breaker for cross-region fallback throttling).

Quick checks to reproduce locally (dev):
- Run small cluster, deploy embed model with artificial memory leak, trigger load with hey/fortio, observe router decisions via /internal/debug and confirm fallback behavior.
- Test new weight smoothing algorithm in PR-429 across synthetic spike patterns.

Raw snippets/notes from Slack & console: 
- "15:29 @Ethan: seeing model-unavailable errors, routing to us-east1 for 15% of traffic"
- Console screenshot notes: fallback_count(route=r-8f2c)=112 over 10m, avg latency (fallback)=420ms vs eu-west baseline 70ms.

Next meeting: post-incident sync scheduled 2025-11-05 14:00 UTC. Invitees: eng-serving-runtime, infra, routing, oncall rotation.

If copying: please preserve request ids and timestamps (I pasted several request ids to infra channel). This doc is a scratchpad - will turn into formal postmortem skeleton after sync.

Misc references: PR-429 (weight smoothing), INC-3421, confluence:Smart-Routing-Design-v2.

End of notes.
